EXTRACTION_METHOD_CORRECTION.criticism: Cropping sprites out of a composited framebuffer is a shortcut. A framebuffer crop bakes in the background behind the sprite, any blending applied over it, and whatever else was drawn at those pixels. It is a PICTURE of the asset, not the asset.
what_was_done_that_way: skull_white and skull_red - cropped, then background keyed out by colour threshold
slot_circle_purple - same, and the other three ring colours were generated from it by recolouring rather than extracted
EXTRACTION_METHOD_CORRECTION.why_it_is_wrong: The keying threshold is a judgement call, so edge pixels are guesswork. Anti-aliased or blended edges keep background contamination. And the palette is whatever survived compositing, not the palette the ROM actually assigns.
EXTRACTION_METHOD_CORRECTION.the_correct_source: The OAM entry gives tile index, palette index and size. The tile data lives in the OBJ VRAM bank and the palette in OBJ palette memory. Both are already captured in every GPU dump - vram_*.bin and palette.bin sit beside state.json. Decoding tile index plus palette index yields the exact asset at its exact palette with true transparency, with no thresholds and no guessing.

what_the_oam_gives_us.note: slot 1 ring, palette 4 - the blue player palette

EXTRACTION_METHOD_CORRECTION.status: The framebuffer crops stay in place as an INTERIM so the port renders something closer than a drawn circle, but they are explicitly not final. Every one must be replaced by a VRAM tile decode.
EXTRACTION_METHOD_CORRECTION.next_action: Write a decoder: read the OAM entry, take tile index and size, pull the 4bpp tile rows from the OBJ VRAM bank in the dump, index them through the given OBJ palette, and emit RGBA with colour 0 transparent. That is the same path the hardware takes and it needs no thresholds at all.

PROPER_EXTRACTION_WORKING.method: The hardware path, not a screenshot crop. Each OAM entry names a tile index, a palette index and a size. The tile rows are read 4bpp from the sub-engine OBJ VRAM bank and indexed through the OBJ palette at 0x600 in the palette dump. Colour index 0 is transparent by definition, so there is no threshold and no guessing at edges.

HEART_ANIMATION_CORRECTION.earlier_error: An earlier entry said "The HUD hearts DO NOT ANIMATE" and the animation tick was removed entirely. That over-corrected. The pickup atlas was indeed wrong - those tilted capsules were model 2634 / animation 2635, the spinning world pickup - but removing all animation was also wrong.
HEART_ANIMATION_CORRECTION.the_truth: On the DS the RIGHTMOST heart, the one representing current health, does an expanding beating animation. So the HUD hearts do animate, just not by spinning: a single heart pulses, and only the one at the current health boundary.
what_that_implies: The animation is per-heart, not per-row - three static hearts and one beating.
Which heart beats moves as health changes, so it is driven by the health value at +0x6B6, not by a fixed index.
It is a scale or size pulse, not a frame-by-frame atlas walk.
HEART_ANIMATION_CORRECTION.how_to_find_it: Capture the DS in-match top screen across consecutive frames and diff the heart row. A pulsing heart changes pixels while its neighbours do not, which isolates both the affected heart and the pulse period. The driver can hold a match steady while dumps are taken, and the earlier work already showed ANIM_TICK runs at 30Hz so the period will be in 30Hz ticks.
HEART_ANIMATION_CORRECTION.status: OPEN. The port currently draws four static hearts, which is closer than four spinning pickups but still not right.

DIGIT_STRIP_OPEN.why_it_matters: The kill and death counters currently use a font. The DS draws them from this strip, so the numbers are the wrong glyphs even though the positions are right.

DIGIT_STRIP_RESOLVED.the_old_plan_was_wrong: The plan was to slice a 119x21 image on a ~12px pitch because an automatic column split only found four groups. Both the image and the pitch were the mistake. That image was a render of map rows 24 and 25 of sub BG1, which sit at y192..207 - below the 192px screen. It is a parked tile bank, not something drawn, and rendering it as a picture and then cutting it up was the same shortcut as cropping a framebuffer.
DIGIT_STRIP_RESOLVED.what_it_actually_is: Ten glyphs in the sub BG1 tile set at char base 3, each two tiles stacked: 178+n on top of 190+n, drawn through BG palette row 5. So 8 wide and 16 tall, gold with a black outline. The guessed pitch would have been wrong in both axes.
DIGIT_STRIP_RESOLVED.how_it_was_found: Read the tilemap at screen base 22 rather than looking at pixels. Rows 24 and 25 hold the run 178..187 over 190..199, which is the bank; scanning the visible rows for those same tile numbers finds where they are used.

TOP_SCREEN_HUD_DECODED.summary: The top-screen HUD is main-engine BG1, decoded from tiles. This replaces the last cropped sprite in the port.
TOP_SCREEN_HUD_DECODED.why_oam_main_was_empty: DISPCNT is 0x00010358. Bit 3 makes BG0 the 3D layer, bits 8-12 read 3 so only BG0 and BG1 are on and OBJ is off entirely. The HUD was never going to be in OAM.
TOP_SCREEN_HUD_DECODED.where_the_tiles_live: VRAMCNT puts banks F and G on main BG, F at 0x06000000 and G at 0x06004000, 16KB each. Concatenating them in that order gives the 32KB the engine sees. BG1 runs char base 0 and screen base 0, so the map occupies the first 2KB and usable tile numbers start at 64.

beat_animation.observation_was_right: An earlier claim that the HUD hearts do not animate was wrong. They do. The rightmost heart, the one representing current health, expands and contracts.
beat_animation.evidence: Fourteen samples across seven in-match dumps. The first three hearts were f0 in every one. The fourth was f1 in four dumps (arena, cam, cam2, mat2) and f0 in the other three (anchor, mat, menuframe). Both DS instances agreed in every single dump, so the pulse runs off a global timer rather than per player, and the duty cycle is close to even. f2 was never caught in a sample.
beat_animation.still_unverified: The period. Snapshots cannot give it. A write watchpoint on the map entries for the fourth heart - 0x060000CC at ty3 tx12 and 0x0600018C at ty4 tx12 - would give it directly, as the gap between writes. The port currently runs a 30-tick cycle at even duty, which matches the observed ratio but is not measured.
beat_animation.also_unverified: The dark frame has never been seen in use, because every dump so far is at full health. The port shows a lost heart as the dark frame rather than removing it, on the reasoning that the quad would not be worth its tile space otherwise. Needs a capture taken after taking a hit.
beat_animation.rom_scan_negative: The ARM9 holds no static table of the heart tile quads. Searched arm9_decompressed.bin for 66/67/74/75, 68/69/76/77, 70/71/78/79 and 72/73/80/81 as halfword runs, both bare and with the palette-1 map bits, and all eight patterns are absent. So the map entries are computed at runtime from a base tile plus a frame index, or the whole 2KB map is staged in RAM and DMAed.
beat_animation.how_to_measure_the_period: Sample rather than watchpoint. A write watchpoint on 0x060000CC only fires if the CPU writes the map, and the ROM scan suggests it may be DMAed instead. Adding a per-frame sample to GPUDump.cpp - read main BG VRAM offset 0xCC, log the tile number against the frame counter - works either way and gives the period straight off the transition gaps. Log for a few hundred frames of a live match.

PORT_MATCHES_DS_BIT_EXACT.what: The top-screen heart row in the port is bit-exact against the DS BG1 layer.
PORT_MATCHES_DS_BIT_EXACT.method: Cropped each 16x16 heart cell from both out/work/bg_layers/main_bg1_char0_screen0.png and out/work/godot_ui_capture/04_jabbas_tower_boba_hud.png and diffed over the DS layer alpha mask.
PORT_MATCHES_DS_BIT_EXACT.result: All four cells, max channel difference 0 and mean 0.00. Cells 0-2 have 146 opaque pixels (the f0 normal frame) and cell 3 has 204 (the f1 beat frame), matching the DS dump exactly - including which frame the pulsing heart was on.

was_wrong_two_ways: Position: RING_CENTRE was (25.5, 28.0). Measured off a real in-match DS frame (out/work/gpudump_arena/inst0/screen0.bin, read as BGRA) the annulus spans x8..43 y6..41 - 36x36 centred on (25.5, 23.5). The port drew it four pixels low.
Asset: it was draw_circle plus draw_arc. The DS row profile across the annulus is a hard 10/14/10; the port produced a soft 9/15/19. Synthesised against hard-edged.
TOP_SCREEN_RING_CORRECTED.the_real_asset: out/exported/godot_ui/slot_circles/circle_<colour>.png, ROM asset 621 - a blue annulus around a pale lavender disc, which is exactly what the frame shows. The same asset already backed the bottom-screen slot rings, so the top screen was the odd one out.
TOP_SCREEN_RING_CORRECTED.scaling: The asset canvas is 40x40 with a 38x38 opaque extent, and the DS puts that extent on screen at 36x36. Drawing the whole canvas into Rect2(8, 6, 37.895, 37.895) lands the opaque part exactly on x8..43 y6..41.
TOP_SCREEN_RING_CORRECTED.where_it_comes_from: Not a sprite. Main DISPCNT is 0x00010358, so OBJ is off and only BG0 (the 3D layer) and BG1 are enabled - and BG1 holds nothing but the four hearts. The portrait and its ring are textured 3D geometry in BG0, which is why the DS can scale them freely and why they never appear in an OAM dump. This also settles that the DS top screen contains exactly two HUD elements: the ring with its portrait, and the four hearts. Nothing else.

STARFIELD_IS_TWO_SCROLLING_LAYERS.was_wrong: The touch screen starfield was one static 256x192 still (starfield_bg2.png) drawn at the origin with no scroll. Its stars did not line up with a real DS frame - 334 of 2628 background-band pixels differed against out/work/gpudump_arena/inst0/screen1.bin.
STARFIELD_IS_TWO_SCROLLING_LAYERS.what_it_actually_is: Sub BG2 and BG3, both char base 0, screen bases 30 and 31. BG3 has the lower priority number so it draws on top of BG2. Decoding both and applying the captured scroll offset (BG2 xpos 135) cut the mismatch to 192 px.

they_scroll.evidence: xpos across consecutive dump frames, 60 frames apart: BG2 1376, 1388, 1400, 1412 and BG3 1721, 1736, 1751, 1766. Holds identically in gpudump_snd2 and gpudump_cam2.
they_scroll.rates: BG2 +12 per 60 frames = 0.2 px/frame; BG3 +15 per 60 frames = 0.25 px/frame.
they_scroll.meaning: Two layers moving at different rates is a parallax field. A single static image cannot reproduce it, which also explains the 192 px residue - a still only matches on the one frame it was taken from.
they_scroll.direction: The hardware samples map column (screen_x + xpos), so a rising xpos moves the field left across the screen.

STARFIELD_IS_TWO_SCROLLING_LAYERS.assets: godot/assets/ui_rom/starfield_far.png (BG2) and starfield_near.png (BG3), exported at the full 256x256 map size so they wrap.
STARFIELD_IS_TWO_SCROLLING_LAYERS.wired: arena_bottom_screen.gd draws both, each blitted twice one wrap apart to cover the seam, advanced in emulator-frame units at 60Hz.

PALETTE_EXPANSION_WAS_WRONG.severity: Affected every asset extracted so far - 31 files.
PALETTE_EXPANSION_WAS_WRONG.what_was_wrong: Every extractor expanded a 5-bit DS colour channel as v * 255 // 31. That is not what the hardware pipeline does and not what melonDS does when it builds the framebuffer these assets are checked against.
PALETTE_EXPANSION_WAS_WRONG.the_correct_formula: From GPU2D_Soft.cpp:296-305 the internal channel is 6-bit (the 5-bit palette entry doubled), it is shifted into the top 6 bits of the byte, and the top 2 bits are replicated into the bottom 2: out8 = (v6 << 2) | (v6 >> 4) with v6 = v5 << 1, which reduces to (v5 << 3) | (v5 >> 3).
PALETTE_EXPANSION_WAS_WRONG.consequence: Nothing extracted was ever pure white - the DS white is 251. The error was found by comparing background luminance histograms between the port and a real DS frame: the DS bucket sat at 56 and 73 where the port sat at 57 and 74, and the DS maximum was 251 where the port reached 255.
PALETTE_EXPANSION_WAS_WRONG.how_it_was_fixed: tools/fix_asset_palettes.py remaps in place - each of the 32 wrong values maps to exactly one correct value. Verified equivalent to re-extraction: after remapping, all four heart assets diff to zero against a freshly extracted layer using the corrected formula. The three extractors (extract_bg_layers, extract_oam_sprites, reconstruct_screen) are patched too.
PALETTE_EXPANSION_WAS_WRONG.files_not_remapped: 4 files hold channel values outside the 32-value set, so they did not come from this pipeline and remapping them would be wrong: heart.png (the superseded crop, now unused), signal_bars.png, and two others. signal_bars.png is still a framebuffer crop and remains to be extracted properly.

TOP_SCREEN_PORTRAIT_GEOMETRY.reported: Portraits floated above the ring border on the HUD.
TOP_SCREEN_PORTRAIT_GEOMETRY.was: PORTRAIT_DISC 28, positioned by centring on RING_CENTRE, which put the rect at (11.5, 9.5) with its bottom edge at y37.5 against a ring inner edge near y39.
TOP_SCREEN_PORTRAIT_GEOMETRY.now: 32x32 at (10, 8). Measured off a real DS frame: the annulus spans x8..43 y6..41 and the disc content inside it spans x10..41 y8..39.
TOP_SCREEN_PORTRAIT_GEOMETRY.cross_check: This matches the bottom screen, where OAM is exact: ring 40x40 at (5,5) and portrait 32x32 at (8,8), an inset of 3. The top ring canvas starts at x6.941, so an origin of 10 is the same inset of about 3. Both screens share the relationship, which is a good sign the top-screen figure is right rather than fitted.
TOP_SCREEN_PORTRAIT_GEOMETRY.REMAINING: The rect is now correct but the portrait still under-fills it. The port's portrait sources carry transparent margins - the extracted DS OAM portraits measure only 24x24 of content inside their 32x32 sprite - so the drawn head is smaller than the DS's even at the right rect and size. Closing that needs the per-character portrait as the DS composites it rather than a render with padding. Only Boba Fett and Greedo have been captured as OAM sprites so far; the other eight hunters need captures with those characters selected.
TOP_SCREEN_PORTRAIT_GEOMETRY.VERIFIED: Fixed and confirmed against a matched-camera DS frame. Over the disc interior (716 px) and the annulus (344 px), ZERO pixels differ by more than 16, mean difference 2.9 and max 4 - and that residual is the 3D-rendering difference already known for the ring, not a placement error. The portrait no longer floats.
TOP_SCREEN_PORTRAIT_GEOMETRY.measurement_correction: An earlier follow-up measurement reported the port at 30x27 against the DS 32x32 and concluded the portrait still under-filled because the source sprites carry transparent margins. That was a BAD MASK, not a real difference - a saturation threshold that clipped the darker portrait pixels. Masking properly, and then diffing the two frames directly, shows them matching. The under-fill claim was wrong and the note about needing per-character OAM portraits does not apply here.
